CHROMIUM: ath10k: Add adjacent wlan radio interference detecting interface Some platforms integrate several radios together. When one radio wants to spectral scan the current channel, the adjacent radio's activity will introduce some interference in the spectral scan result. To combat the problem, enable the FW to set a special mark within the spectral scan results. Using such a mark, the user who is processing the data can identify whether the data has been introduced by the interference of the adjacent radio during that period. The user can interpret more accurate spectral scan results with the given marks where interference occurred. This technique requires the preconditions that the scanning and adjacent radio have some physical connection to make them aware of each other's activity from within the FW layer, and the FW claimed supporting this capability. to enable this feature, execute: echo 1 > /sys/kernel/debug/ieee80211/phyX/ath10k/adjacent_wlan_interfrc Then run the spectral scan steps. To check whether the spectral scan data be interfered, execute: cat /sys/kernel/debug/ieee80211/phyX/ath10k/adjacent_wlan_interfrc INTERFRC DETECT FOR SPEC SCAN: Enable/Disable 5G_interference: X/0 2G_Interference: X/0 X means the interference number in the scan period, 0 means no interference. These counters will be reset when next round spectral scan be triggered BUG=chrome-os-partner:51964 TEST=ran iperf after connecting a wifi client with our AP (cherry picked from commit f3262e6d20cf91ad964b565128a6e16976e01cf2) (source: wireless-3.18) Change-Id: I9259717906406b30e3ee4ab2cbdc7c2137d8f5a1 Signed-off-by: Yanbo Li <yanbol@qca.qualcomm.com> Signed-off-by: Mohammed Shafi Shajakhan <mohammed@codeaurora.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/340720 Commit-Ready: Yixiang Li <yixiang@google.com> Tested-by: Yixiang Li <yixiang@google.com> Reviewed-by: Srinivasa duvvuri <sduvvuri@chromium.org>

CHROMIUM: ath10k: Ignore the adjacent radio's activity when surveying a channel The overall goal for a scanning radio is to evaluate the outside radio environment. Some platforms integrate several radios together. When one radio wants to survey the current channel, the adjacent radio's activity will make this survey result inaccurate. Switcher can be used to enable the FW to ignore the survey time slot when the adjacent radio is active, especially for TX. This skipped scan approach will make the survey result more accurate. This technique requires a precondition that the scanning and adjacent radio have some physical connection to make them aware of each other's activity from within the FW layer, and the FW claimed supporting this capability. BUG=chrome-os-partner:51964 TEST=ran traffic with wifi client connected echo 2 > /sys/kernel/debug/ieee80211/phyX/ath10k/adjacent_wlan_interfrc Then run the survey scan and dump the stastics: iw dev wifiX survey dump The TX&RX counter showed already deducted the time slot be interfered To check whether the feature is enabled, execute: cat /sys/kernel/debug/ieee80211/phyX/ath10k/adjacent_wlan_interfrc INTERFRC DETECT FOR SURVEY SCAN: Enable/Disable (cherry picked from commit 825defe22caa71caa1e69b1234967d2e66319952) (source: wireles-4.2/kernel v3.14) Change-Id: I2478e1939d8934f57c980ecc8e8037433fc43dae Signed-off-by: Yanbo Li <yanbol@qca.qualcomm.com> Signed-off-by: Mohammed Shafi Shajakhan <mohammed@codeaurora.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/340722 Commit-Ready: Yixiang Li <yixiang@google.com> Tested-by: Yixiang Li <yixiang@google.com> Reviewed-by: Srinivasa duvvuri <sduvvuri@chromium.org>

CHROMIUM: ath10k: Supply the 64bits channel survey counters The previous TX & RX cycle counters used to report the channel survey are 32 bits, it will wraparound after reach 0xffffffff, the wraparound happens in a short cycle (24 seconds), if the user wants survey > 24 seconds TX & RX counters on a specific channel, the counters will overflow again and again which make the long time survey impossible. There is a new WMI message be added to access the counter in 64bits format, it will greatly extent the overflow time, and userspace will have enough time to handle such case by calculate the counter difference between two samples. The userspace application could call the NL80211_CMD_GET_SURVEY to get the 64 bits counter survey result of currently channel, the result also can be gotten via the available command "iw station survey dump" known limitation: 1: Not be tested for multichannel support scenario 2: Background scan at hostapd AP mode need verificaiton BUG=chrome-os-partner:51964 TEST=ran iperf traffic with wifi client connected The userspace application could call the NL80211_CMD_GET_SURVEY to get the 64 bits counter survey result of currently channel, the result also can be gotten via the available command "iw station survey dump"a (cherry picked from commit 002c1d21718ec37ee298d978b6c1bf62586fe905) (source: wireless-4.2/v3.14) Change-Id: I9065d0f4671e374ad06e1953b83e354509b3eeb2 Signed-off-by: Yanbo Li <yanbol@qca.qualcomm.com> Signed-off-by: Mohammed Shafi Shajakhan <mohammed@codeaurora.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/340723 Commit-Ready: Yixiang Li <yixiang@google.com> Tested-by: Yixiang Li <yixiang@google.com> Reviewed-by: Srinivasa duvvuri <sduvvuri@chromium.org>

CHROMIUM: ath10k: Add sanity check on survey data returned from FW. This implements a Workaround for 3 issues 41610, 40927, 41688. Issue 41610: busy_duration_millis measured by the Aux Radio spike to ~48805. Issue 40927: ACS noise floor frequently jumps to -48 Issue 41688: Rx Duration reported by the 2.4GHz radio is much higher than measurement duration. Until these issues are fixed, sanity check and filter out the data using the following checks. (channel_time_tx + channel_time_rx) <= channel_time_busy channel_time_busy <= channel_time noise_value < -60 . Scan and dump survey data. Check from kernel log and from output of survey dump that the invalid data is ignored/filtered out by the driver. BUG=chrome-os-partner:51964 TEST=ran iperf with a wifi client connected (cherry picked from commit c869cd0c09e33e1d17fbf36d91276e865208091e) (source: wireless-3.18) Change-Id: I20555e319a60f2c787da07e6a565d61307548aa7 Signed-off-by: Yanbo Li <yanbol@qca.qualcomm.com> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/340724 Commit-Ready: Yixiang Li <yixiang@google.com> Tested-by: Yixiang Li <yixiang@google.com> Reviewed-by: Srinivasa duvvuri <sduvvuri@chromium.org>

CHROMIUM: ath10k: Instrument driver to better show problems gathering channel load These changes are being submitted in order to get them to beta channel to help diagnose where the system is breaking when we fail to get channel survey results on one of the main radios. It triggers so infrequently that we need a large test group. Once triggered, it does not affect traffic on the device, but it does not seem to self-resolve and it prevents Waveguide from making channel change recommendations. This CL does not change any functionality. It merely adds logging. This CL will be reverted prior to public release. (cherry picked from commit "bda3ac02d03c30f8f91c4987bc3b413b5ff71c21") (source wireless-4.2/v3.14) TEST=ran iperf with a wifi client connected BUG=chrome-os-partner:51964 Change-Id: Iba88d34c679fa9a76a65902e2a044b4e0d07013f Signed-off-by: walker <walker@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/340733 Commit-Ready: Yixiang Li <yixiang@google.com> Tested-by: Yixiang Li <yixiang@google.com> Reviewed-by: Srinivasa duvvuri <sduvvuri@chromium.org>

CHROMIUM: ath10k: fix rx_channel during hw reconfigure Upon firmware assert, restart work will be triggered so that mac80211 will reconfigure the driver. An issue is reported that after restart work, survey dump data do not contain in-use (SURVEY_INFO_IN_USE) infor for operating channel. During reconfigure, since mac80211 already has valid channel context for given radio, channel context iteration return num_chanctx > 0. Hence rx_channel is always NULL. Fix this by assigning channel context to rx_channel when driver restart is in progress. (cherry picked from commit 6ceadec1df28c3938237358fdde5468afcd9872d) (source wireless-4.2/v3.14) BUG=chrome-os-partner:51964 TEST=ran iperf with a client connected Change-Id: I95956760762b3cfa2d2a61b2d8b4f88b8c6e6f6d Signed-off-by: Rajkumar Manoharan <rmanohar@qti.qualcomm.com> Signed-off-by: Mohammed Shafi Shajakhan <mohammed@codeaurora.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/340734 Commit-Ready: Yixiang Li <yixiang@google.com> Tested-by: Yixiang Li <yixiang@google.com> Reviewed-by: Srinivasa duvvuri <sduvvuri@chromium.org>

gru: enable pp1500 and pp3000 rails as soon as possible The idea is that they stay low unless we know that we booted from SPI flash. As this code runs in SPI flash - it is ok to turn these rails on as soon as possible, and pp3000 rail it is essential for UART to work. Kevin rev1 and Gru designs are going to be using these pins to control these rails. Kevin rev1 had those GPIO pins routed to two chip enable signals, it is save to assert them high.
